subject: Career
title: Why Most People Don't Negotiate
description: Learn Why Most People Don't Negotiate in one minute.

hook.text: Only 39% of workers negotiate their salary. The other 61% accept the first offer.

buildup.text: Fear of rejection, gratitude for the offer, and not knowing how — these keep people silent.

discovery.text: But 85% of those who do negotiate get something more. The odds are overwhelmingly in your favor.

twist.text: Not negotiating costs an average of $600K over a career due to compounding base differences.

climax.text: The company expects negotiation. A budget range already exists. Your silence just saves them money.

punchline.text: The most expensive word in your career is 'okay.'

quiz.question: What percentage of workers negotiate their salary?

details.summary: Studies show that roughly 60 percent of workers accept an initial job offer without negotiating. Fear of rejection, discomfort with conflict, and a lack of market information all contribute to this passive acceptance, which can cost hundreds of thousands of dollars across a career.
details.whyItMatters: Even a single $5,000 increase at age 25 compounds to more than $600,000 in lifetime earnings. Not negotiating is the single most expensive silence in a career.
takeaways: Most workers accept the first offer they receive
Fear of confrontation is the top barrier to negotiating
A single early negotiation can compound to six figures

faq.question: Is it true that employers expect candidates to negotiate?
faq.answer: Yes. Many hiring managers build a negotiation buffer into their initial offer, typically between five and fifteen percent. Candidates who accept without discussion may actually be leaving expected money on the table.

faq.question: What if the employer rescinds the offer when I try to negotiate?
faq.answer: Rescinded offers due to polite, well-reasoned counter-proposals are extremely rare. Employers invest thousands in recruiting; withdrawing an offer over a professional conversation would undermine their own hiring process.
